clue.text: Support of the French purchased by sweetheart

indicators.note: a purchase is a grip, so being purchased by something is being gripped and held inside it

parts.note: petal is an affectionate British form of address, like sweetheart
des is French for 'of the' (plural)

explanation.surface: Someone's darling has bought a French piece of support, perhaps furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchased by' does not mean bought here: a purchase is a grip, so it signals one piece held inside another. Petal is a British endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base on which a statue or column stands, so it is a support.

clue.text: Lyrical American writer surmounts boundless criticism

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

indicators.note: boundless removes the letters at both ends of the word

parts.note: stick is informal for criticism, as in giving someone stick

explanation.surface: An American poet tops a pile of endless critiques.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boundless' strips STICK to TIC; 'surmounts' puts POE above it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic means having the qualities of poetry, so it is lyrical in style.

clue.text: Party piece involves right geezer

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: involves means the bit wraps round the next letter

parts.note: a tad is a small piece or bit

explanation.surface: A party piece performed by a right old character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party piece' reads as a set performance but splits into two words; 'involves' sets the R inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Geezer is slang for an old man, and a dotard is an old man gone feeble in mind.

clue.text: Army supporting fight for ancient city

indicators.note: supporting means sitting below in a down clue, so the army goes under the fight

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do
TA is the Territorial Army, the British army reserve

explanation.surface: An army backing a war for a city of the ancient world.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a city-state of ancient Greece, famous for its soldiers.

clue.text: Say some sounds sounding similar, say?

definitions.text: Say some sounds sounding similar, say?

parts.words: Say some sounds sounding similar, say
parts.note: the clue describes itself, repeating the starting consonant over and over as it does

explanation.surface: Instructions to speak several matching sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is its own example: say, some, sounds, sounding, similar, say all start with S.
explanation.definitionFit: To alliterate is to use words that begin with the same consonant sound in succession.

clue.text: Friends maybe gather scoff, almost over …

parts.note: a committee or court sits when it gathers in session

indicators.note: over says the shortened word is turned round
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to scoff is to mock

explanation.surface: Friends meet to gather and jeer, the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter and 'over' turns what remains. The ellipsis joins this clue to the next only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends is the famous American television situation comedy, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Make United popular team rising around season

indicators.note: around says the popular team surrounds the season

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: XI is a team of eleven, as in cricket or football
a term is a period of time, a season

explanation.surface: Making Manchester United a popular team as it climbs during the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the team in this down clue; 'around' wraps both pieces round the season. 'United' is not the football club but the object of 'Make'.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermix is to blend things together, which is to make them united.

clue.text: Purveyor of wicked articles?

parts.note: wicked here means having a wick, so the articles are candles and their seller is a candle-maker

explanation.surface: A dealer in evil goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' looks like evil but means fitted with a wick.
explanation.definitionFit: A chandler originally made and sold candles, the classic items that have wicks.

clue.text: Fancy woman, very French, embraced by mademoiselle

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside the arms of the next word

parts.note: mademoiselle is French for Miss
tres is French for very

explanation.surface: A very French young woman is courted by a mademoiselle.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy woman is an old informal term for a lover or kept woman, which a mistress is.

clue.text: … means suppressing initially rumbling guts

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down inside, so the first word encloses the letter

parts.note: to entail is to mean or involve as a consequence

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word rumbling

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, a rumbling stomach is being held down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing' puts R, the first letter of 'rumbling', inside ENTAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the intestines or internal organs, which are colloquially called guts.

clue.text: Secures hatch on board

indicators.note: on board a ship is inside it, so on here sets the hatch between the ship's letters

parts.note: the board in on board is a ship, SS being the abbreviation for steamship
a trap or trapdoor is a hatch

explanation.surface: Someone battens down a hatch on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the old convention of putting a word inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: To strap something is to fasten it with a belt, so straps is a verb meaning secures.

clue.text: Frailty occasionally waylaid by raging bug

indicators.note: something waylaid is stopped and held by another, so it sits inside that word

parts.note: raging means furious, irate

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of Frailty

explanation.surface: A weakness is ambushed by a furious virus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of Frailty; 'waylaid by' puts them inside. 'bug' looks like a germ but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is informally to annoy them, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: More natural Conservative comparatively blue

parts.note: blue means smutty, rude, so more blue is ruder

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician is both more natural and more smutty than others.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is also the Conservative party colour, a misleading echo; here it means indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude oil is natural, unrefined, so cruder means rawer or less processed.

clue.text: Pervert said to be in ruin

indicators.note: to be in tells us the spoken word goes inside the ruin word

parts.note: demise means downfall, ruin
oral means spoken, said

explanation.surface: A deviant is reported to be in ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a homophone signal but means spoken, and 'to be in' is the container signal. Pervert is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To demoralise in its older sense is to corrupt morals, so it means to pervert.

clue.text: Eats in suits first off displaying gluttony

indicators.note: in places the eating word inside the trimmed word
first off removes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: if something suits you it agrees with you
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone dining in a business suit shows how greedy they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' drops the opening letter of the suits word; 'in' takes the eating word inside it. 'suits' is a verb, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Greediness is excessive desire for food, which is exactly gluttony.

clue.text: Hamlet character more wretched about delay

indicators.note: about places the first word around the second

parts.note: viler means more wretched
lag means delay

explanation.surface: A character in Hamlet grows more wretched in his procrastination.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet is a small settlement, not Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: A villager is a resident of a small rural place such as a hamlet.

clue.text: Discharge from volcano I suffered climbing

indicators.note: climbing says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A volcano eruption hurt me as I climbed it.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'from' as a link; it signals the hidden letters taken from the phrase. 'climbing' reads them upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Effusion is a pouring out of liquid or gas, a discharge.

clue.text: Train connected to stiff carriage?

parts.note: re means about or connected to, as in a letter heading
a stiff is slang for a corpse, and a hearse is the vehicle that carries it

explanation.surface: A train linked to a rigid railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' and 'carriage' suggest the railway; Train is the verb, practise.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise or drill, as actors do, so it means to train.

clue.text: Stress beginning to lessen during illness

indicators.note: during says the letter comes within the illness word

parts.note: an infection is an illness

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of lessen

explanation.surface: Anxiety starts to ease while someone is unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives L from 'lessen'; 'during' sets it inside INFECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflection is the rise and fall or emphasis in speech, so it means stress in the vocal sense.

clue.text: Falling star made the other all gutted

indicators.note: gutted removes the insides, leaving only the outer letters of each word

explanation.surface: A celebrity's decline left everyone devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all gutted' looks like despair but keeps the outsides of made, the and other.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a shooting star, a fragment burning up as it falls through the atmosphere.

clue.text: Fingers will be number with onset of syndrome

parts.note: a digit is a single numeral, a number

indicators.note: onset of takes the first letter of syndrome

explanation.surface: Fingers will be counted when symptoms begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits are fingers or toes, the anatomical term for them.

clue.text: Watchful missing last of English ways

indicators.note: missing last of says the final occurrence of the letter is dropped

parts.note: all eyes is an idiom for watchful, paying full attention

explanation.surface: A careful observer misses the last of English customs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of English' is not H: it drops the last E from ALL EYES.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleys are narrow lanes or passages, so they are ways or paths.

clue.text: Hardy perennial?

parts.note: read as a person, Oliver Hardy's perennial partner in the comedy double act; read as a plant, a tough evergreen bush

explanation.surface: A garden plant that comes back every year.
explanation.walkthrough: A hardy perennial is a plant; read as a person, Hardy's perennial partner was Laurel of Laurel and Hardy, the comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: The laurel is a hardy evergreen shrub, and Laurel was Hardy's constant comedy partner.

clue.text: China form perhaps turned bodily

parts.note: china means mate, from Cockney rhyming slang china plate

indicators.note: turned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a form is a hare's resting place, an example of a lair

explanation.surface: A piece of china or porcelain form has been shaped on a wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' and 'form' suggest pottery; china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), and a hare's form is its lair, which 'turned' makes RIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Material as an adjective means physical or relating to the body, as opposed to spiritual.

clue.text: Swelling, the thing's covered in blood

indicators.note: covered in says the item sits within the blood word

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
it stands for the thing

explanation.surface: A grisly swelling is smeared in blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A goitre is an enlargement of the thyroid gland, seen as a lump in the neck.

clue.text: Home provided in retirement lodge

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: provided means if, as in provided that
to lodge is to live somewhere, to reside

explanation.surface: A pensioner's home in retirement is a lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' reverses only the short word; 'lodge' is a verb, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside stands for home life, as in the cosy domestic hearth.

clue.text: Gets up without nightclothes originally and bathes

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the rising word goes round the letter

parts.note: rises means gets up

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of nightclothes

explanation.surface: Someone gets up and washes without pyjamas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: RISES goes round N, the first of 'nightclothes'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly with water, a near synonym of bathe.

clue.text: Some imitation Euros issued creating disorder

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fake euro notes put into circulation are causing chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental condition marked by anxiety, a psychological disorder that troubles the mind.
